title: What Person in Charge (PIC) certification and food handler training does Dubai Municipality require?
seoTitle: Dubai Municipality PIC and food training
description: Dubai Municipality PIC rules: who must hold a PIC certificate, how many per shift, five year validity, food handler training hours, refreshers and records.
shortAnswer: Dubai Municipality's Food Code requires every food establishment in Dubai to employ at least one full time, on site Person in Charge (PIC) certified in food safety, with a certified PIC present on every shift where high risk, ready to eat or raw food is prepared. PIC certificates are valid for five years. All food handlers must be trained before they start work in food areas, using trainers and materials approved by the Food Safety Department.
keyTakeaways: Section 3.1.1 of the Dubai Food Code requires at least one full time, on site certified PIC per establishment, and a certified PIC on all shifts in food service businesses handling high risk, ready to eat or raw food.
A PIC certificate is valid for five years. If a PIC leaves, the establishment has 30 days to designate a replacement, who must be certified within 45 days.
Guideline DM-FSD-GU64 (issue 2, August 31, 2023) sets the number and level of PICs by business type, for example one Advanced PIC per shift in each hotel kitchen.
Food handlers must be trained on basic food safety before they start work unless already qualified, with minimum course lengths of 3 or 5 learning hours and a 70% pass mark.

The Food Code (2013) calls for a refresher after one year, while GU64 (2023) requires food handler refreshers every three years or when competency deteriorates; confirm current practice with the Food Safety Department.
jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates: Emirate of Dubai
regulator: Dubai Municipality, Food Safety Department (Environment, Health and Safety Agency)
appliesTo: All food establishments licensed in the Emirate of Dubai, including restaurants, cafeterias, hotels, caterers, supermarkets, bakeries, butchers, school and hospital kitchens, manufacturers and food traders
Persons in Charge (PICs) who supervise food safety in those establishments
All food handlers, and staff managing food related services such as buffet counters and food delivery
Internal and external training centers, trainers and certification bodies delivering programs mandated by the Food Safety Department

sections.heading: Which Dubai Municipality instruments set PIC and food handler training rules?

blocks.text: Two Dubai Municipality documents carry the training obligations: the [Dubai Food Code](https://dmpmedia.dm.gov.ae/uploads/2024/10/Food-Code-2013-English.pdf), which sets the duty to employ a certified PIC (section 3.1) and to train food handlers (section 6), and the [Requirements for Integrated Training Management System for Food Establishments](https://dmpmedia.dm.gov.ae/uploads/2024/02/3.-DM-FSD-GU64-Requirements-for-Integrated-Training-Management-System-for-Food-Establishments-2.pdf) (document reference DM-FSD-GU64, issue 2, dated August 31, 2023), which turns those duties into operating rules for training centers, trainers, assessments and certificates.

GU64 states that it applies to "all training programs mandated by the Food Safety Department of Dubai Municipality, including the Person in Charge Certification program", and that it is aligned to Section 6 of the Food Code. Both documents are listed on Dubai Municipality's [food traders and establishments page](https://www.dm.gov.ae/municipality-business/food-traders-establishments/), as at November 2026.

The PIC program is not new. The Food Code's foreword says Dubai Municipality introduced its "proprietary Person In-Charge (PIC) program" in 2010. In a [2020 statement](https://www.dm.gov.ae/dubai-municipality-oversees-more-than-70000-mandatory-pics-in-dubais-food-establishments/), the Municipality said it was overseeing 72,108 mandatory PICs and that PIC training runs at three levels matched to high, medium and low risk establishments.

sections.heading: Who must have a certified Person in Charge, and how many are required?

blocks.text: Every food establishment needs at least one certified PIC, and higher risk food service businesses need one on every shift. Section 3.1.1 of the Food Code sets five rules:

items: All food establishments shall employ at least one full time, on site PIC certified in food safety.
Food service establishments preparing high risk, ready to eat or raw foods shall have at least one certified PIC present during all shifts.
Each PIC must pass a written examination acceptable to the food control department and receives a certificate valid for five years from issue.
The PIC's name should be displayed behind the cash counter or in a place clearly visible to customers.
When a PIC's employment ends, the establishment can take up to 30 days to designate a new PIC, who should enroll in training and be certified within 45 days.

sections.heading: What does a Dubai PIC have to do, and what must the training cover?

blocks.text: The PIC is accountable for day to day food safety and for the training of other staff. Section 3.1.2 of the Food Code requires the PIC to supervise safe food practices, inspect the premises regularly, take corrective action, and ensure that "all employees are trained before they start of work" and that trained employees are competent. Section 6.2 adds that the PIC must periodically assess the effectiveness of training and must keep records of which employees have been trained.

GU64 Annex Table 1 lists the competencies a certified PIC must show, grouped under food safety responsibilities, managing food safety, personal hygiene, operational requirements and food safety management systems. They include knowing the common contributing factors to foodborne illness in Dubai, knowing when to exclude ill employees, using the Foodwatch platform to record daily inspections, delivery checks and corrective actions, and ensuring "the food safety training needs and competencies of staff are met". PICs in school catering, or in businesses making nutritional or health claims, need additional nutrition competencies.

After certification the role is tied to Dubai Municipality's digital systems. GU64 requires the PIC to use Foodwatch for food safety checks and, when an inspector records a violation, to access the e-learning on the Foodwatch app to understand the corrective action. PIC certificates can be withdrawn early if the establishment's food safety performance is poor.

sections.heading: What training must food handlers complete before and after they start work?

blocks.text: Food handlers must be formally trained in food safety, and anyone without a food safety qualification must be trained before starting work in food areas. Section 6.2 of the Food Code says all food handlers "must be formally trained on food safety", extends this where necessary to staff managing food related services such as buffet counters and delivery, and requires training from a trainer approved by the Department.

GU64 sets the operating detail. Training can start without the employee's Emirates ID provided the details are entered within 90 days. Training centers must use approved materials and trainer led sessions, and confirm the trainee understands the language of delivery. Minimum learning hours, excluding breaks, are:

items: Basic Food Safety Program: 3 learning hours
Basic Food Safety Program, Food Service: 5 learning hours
Basic Food Safety for drivers and delivery personnel: 3 learning hours
Refresher program for food handlers who hold the Basic Food Safety Program: 2 learning hours

blocks.text: GU64 Table 4 assigns the course by business type. Restaurants, cafeterias, caterers, hotels, hospital kitchens, schools and bakeries use Basic Food Safety, Food Service, while grocery stores selling only pre-packed food and food trading companies use the standard Basic Food Safety program.

blocks.title: Refresher frequency: two documents, two answers
blocks.text: Section 6.3 of the Food Code (2013) says food handlers "should participate in a refresher or updating course after one year of training". GU64 (2023) says food handlers "must undergo refresher training every three years or when deterioration of food safety competency is noticed", and that Basic Food Safety certificates are issued without a validity date. GU64 is the more recent and more detailed instrument, but an establishment should confirm the expected interval with the Food Safety Department and record which rule its training plan follows.

sections.heading: How are PICs and food handlers assessed and certified?

blocks.text: Every trainee sits a formal, documented assessment after training, and the pass mark is 70%. GU64 requires digital assessment tools approved by the Food Safety Department, prohibits paper based examinations, and allows one re-examination; a candidate who fails twice must repeat the full course. Wrong answers on questions critical to competency, such as illness reporting or handwashing, allow the Department to revoke the qualification and require reassessment.

PIC assessment is held to a higher standard. GU64 requires it to follow ISO/IEC 17024:2012, the international standard for bodies certifying persons, with identity checked at the start of training and again by the examiner. Contact PIC classes are capped at 16 candidates, compared with 20 for other programs. Certificates must carry the candidate's full name, Emirates ID number, course, trainer, training center, completion date and a Foodwatch traceability number, and every qualification must be traceable on Foodwatch.

Training providers carry their own obligations. Trainers need Food Safety Department approval, at least five years of food safety experience including three years supervising food safety in a food establishment, and 30 hours of continuing professional development each year logged on Foodwatch. Training centers must send the Department a six monthly summary showing, per question, the share of trainees who answered correctly on the first attempt.

sections.heading: What evidence should a Dubai food establishment keep for an inspection?

blocks.text: An inspector will expect to see a certified PIC on shift, current certificates traceable on Foodwatch, and training records for every food handler. sections.heading: How does the Dubai PIC compare with similar roles elsewhere?

blocks.text: The Dubai PIC is closest to the certified food protection manager in the US FDA Food Code and the food safety supervisor in Australian states. All three place a trained, examined individual on the premises and make that person responsible for training others. Dubai's model differs in three ways: the number of PICs is set by business type and shift in a published table, the certificate is tied to a government platform (Foodwatch) for daily self inspection, and assessment must follow ISO/IEC 17024.

See [the FDA Food Code certified food protection manager rule](/regulations/fda-food-code-certified-food-protection-manager), the [NSW food safety supervisor requirements](/regulations/nsw-food-safety-supervisor-requirements) and the cross market summary in [food safety training requirements by country](/compare/food-safety-training-requirements-by-country). Abu Dhabi has a separate regime under the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority, covered in [Abu Dhabi food handler training requirements](/regulations/abu-dhabi-food-handler-training-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models the Food Code clauses and the GU64 competency table as obligations linked to roles, shifts and assessment points before any course is written. Where two instruments disagree, as on refresher intervals, both are recorded with their dates so the chosen rule is visible to an inspector and easy to change.

faqs.q: How long is a Dubai Municipality PIC certificate valid?
faqs.a: Five years. Section 3.1.1 of the Food Code says each person passing an acceptable examination receives a certificate valid for five years from the date of issue, and GU64 confirms the five year validity, adding that a certificate can be withdrawn earlier because of poor food safety performance at the establishment.

faqs.q: Can a food handler start work before completing food safety training in Dubai?
faqs.a: Only if the person already holds formal food safety training relevant to the work. GU64 says a person with no food safety qualification must be trained on basic food safety before starting work in food areas. Training may take place before the Emirates ID is issued, provided the details are entered on the system within 90 days.

faqs.q: Can PIC and food safety training be delivered online in Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes, with approval. GU64 allows fully online, blended or trainer led training through a learning management system approved by the Food Safety Department and integrated with Foodwatch. Virtual delivery needs a prior permit, and training centers with a history of noncompliance cannot deliver virtual training.

faqs.q: What happens if a training certificate is issued without the training taking place?
faqs.a: GU64 treats it as fraudulent. Certificates issued to candidates who did not complete the training or assessment, or issued using unapproved trainers, are considered fraudulent and Dubai Municipality will initiate legal action. Trainer approvals are also cancelled for sharing system credentials or misreporting candidate details.

faqs.q: Does the Dubai PIC requirement apply in Abu Dhabi or other emirates?
faqs.a: No. The Food Code and GU64 are Dubai Municipality instruments and apply to food establishments in the Emirate of Dubai. Abu Dhabi food establishments are regulated by the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority, which runs its own mandatory food handler training. Other emirates have their own municipal food control authorities.
